paper: Han S-R et al. 2021, BMC Genomics 22:403 (PMID 34078272) — Arthrobacter sp. PAMC25564 complete genome and CAZymes in cold adaptation

open_questions.q: Do the glycogen/trehalose CAZyme families (GH13_11, GH13_26, GH65, GH77, CBM48) recovered in PAMC25564 actually up-regulate at low temperature, or are they simply present in the genome?
open_questions.basis: The paper's cold-adaptation claim is a genomic-association argument (family presence + counts across comparators). Both the paper and this replication demonstrate the genes exist but neither ties expression or enzyme activity to cold conditions. Correlational genomics cannot distinguish 'cold-relevant' from 'housekeeping carbohydrate metabolism'.
next_steps: RNA-seq of PAMC25564 at growth-limit low temperature (e.g. 4 °C) vs an optimum-temperature control; test differential expression of the six signature families.
Enzyme activity assays of purified GH65 (α-trehalose phosphorylase) and GH13_11 (glycogen debranching) at 4 °C vs 25 °C to test cold-adapted kinetics (kcat/Km temperature profile).
Compare expression response to that of a mesophilic Arthrobacter with the same CAZyme complement to isolate cold-specific regulation from constitutive presence.

open_questions.q: Is the glycogen-plus-trehalose CAZyme signature actually distinctive of Antarctic/psychrophilic Arthrobacter, or is it a general Arthrobacter/Pseudarthrobacter trait?
open_questions.basis: The paper compares against 16–26 complete genomes, but this comparator set is small relative to the current sequenced diversity of the genus, and this replication only spot-verified availability rather than re-running the pan-CAZyme comparison. Whether the signature holds at N=100+ genomes (with proper cold-vs-mesophile stratification) is untested.
next_steps: Assemble a curated set of ≥50 mesophilic Arthrobacter/Pseudarthrobacter and ≥15 cold/polar isolates with complete genomes.
Rerun dbCAN (V13+) uniformly across the set and test for enrichment of GH13_11, GH13_26, GH65, GH77, CBM48 in cold isolates by Fisher's exact / MANOVA on class counts.
Include an outgroup of thermophilic Actinomycetota to strengthen directionality.

open_questions.q: How much of the paper–vs–rerun CAZyme delta (108 vs 102; CE 23→16, CBM 2→9) is dbCAN version drift vs pipeline drift (dbCAN2 3-signature vs HMMER-only)?
open_questions.basis: The paper used dbCAN2's HMMER + Hotpep + DIAMOND overview against a V8-era HMM DB; this replication used HMMER-only against V9. Both variables changed simultaneously because the V8 DB is offline (bcb.unl.edu cyberattack). CBM/CE calls are the most version-sensitive classes in dbCAN, and they are precisely where the delta lives.
next_steps: Once dbCAN2 V8 HMM DB is republished (or recovered from mirrors), rerun HMMER-only vs V8 to isolate DB-version effect from tool-signature effect.
Run the full dbCAN2 3-signature pipeline vs V9 on PAMC25564 to isolate tool-signature effect.
Report a 2×2 (V8/V9 × HMMER-only/3-signature) factorial to attribute the 108→102 delta cleanly.

open_questions.q: Does the current RefSeq re-annotation (RS_2024_05_22: 3,863 genes / 3,718 CDS / 75 pseudo) reflect improved gene-calling for PAMC25564, or an over-call driven by updated pseudogene-detection heuristics?
open_questions.basis: Reproducing the paper's six counts required pinning to the 2019-04-11 GenBank annotation. The 2024 re-annotation drifts materially (especially the pseudogene count 147→75). This matters because future researchers using the latest annotation will see 'different' numbers and may incorrectly conclude the paper is wrong — and because the 'real' gene count of PAMC25564 is genuinely ambiguous between vintages.
next_steps: Diff the two GFF/GBFF annotations feature-by-feature; catalogue where new CDS calls came from (novel small ORFs? merges? splits?) and where pseudogenes were reclassified as intact CDS.
Cross-check ambiguous calls against Prokka and Bakta annotations to identify a consensus core vs annotation-tool-specific calls.
Publish a version-pinning note so downstream cold-adaptation analyses agree on a canonical annotation vintage.

open_questions.q: Are the specific CBM48 and GH13_11 loci in PAMC25564 orthologs of the cold-adapted glycogen-debranching machinery seen in other polar Actinomycetota (e.g. Rhodococcus, Cryobacterium), or are they lineage-specific?
open_questions.basis: CBM48 is a starch/glycogen carbohydrate-binding module frequently paired with GH13 in glycogen-branching / debranching enzymes. The paper flags CBM48 as part of the cold-adaptation signature but does not perform ortholog-level phylogenetic analysis against other cold-adapted bacteria outside Arthrobacter. Whether the cold-adaptation module was inherited, convergent, or horizontally acquired is unresolved.
next_steps: Extract the CBM48-bearing GH13 protein sequences from PAMC25564 and BLAST against a curated set of polar Actinomycetota (Rhodococcus, Cryobacterium, Modestobacter, Rhodoglobus).
Build a gene tree for the GH13_11 subfamily across polar and temperate isolates; compare topology to the species tree to detect HGT vs vertical inheritance.
Test for cold-adaptation signatures at the protein-sequence level (elevated Gly/Ala, reduced Pro/Arg, surface flexibility) in the polar clade vs mesophilic sister clades.
